summary: Describes the architecture of SNMP management frameworks. It is modular: an SNMP engine made of a message processing subsystem, a security subsystem and an access control subsystem, plus one or more applications that sit on top of the engine. This lets the protocol evolve without redoing everything.

eli5.summary: Think of a building plan for network-management software. It says which rooms exist, such as one for reading messages, one for security and one for deciding who may do what, so each can be changed without rebuilding the rest.

questions: what are the parts of an snmp engine
what are the snmpv3 security levels
subtitle: The blueprint that splits an SNMP system into swappable parts: messages, security, access control and applications.

tldr.problem: SNMP had grown through several versions with weak security, especially for changing settings, and each upgrade risked disturbing the whole framework.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3411 defines a vocabulary and a modular layout: an SNMP engine (dispatcher plus message processing, security and access control subsystems) with applications on top, joined by abstract service interfaces.
tldr.outcome: Parts such as message formats or security models can be replaced or added without redoing the rest. It is an Internet Standard (STD 62), obsoletes RFC 2571, and has been updated by RFC 5343 and RFC 5590.

facts.label: Engine parts
facts.value: Dispatcher, message processing, security, access control

today: RFC 3411 is an Internet Standard (STD 62) and has not been obsoleted. It has been updated by RFC 5343 and RFC 5590. It replaced RFC 2571.

sections.title: Why an Architecture for SNMP
sections.content:
RFC 3411 does not define a new wire protocol. It defines a vocabulary and an architecture for describing SNMP Management Frameworks, and it deliberately does not give a general introduction to SNMP or its history.

The goals include reusing earlier work (it builds on SNMPv2u and SNMPv2*, themselves based on SNMPv2p), addressing the need for secure SET support (called the most important deficiency in SNMPv1 and SNMPv2c), keeping SNMP simple and cheap to implement in a minimal form, and making it possible to upgrade portions of SNMP without disrupting an entire framework.

A management system, in these terms, has many nodes whose SNMP entities answer commands and send notifications (traditionally called agents), at least one entity that issues commands or receives notifications (traditionally a manager), and a management protocol between them.
sections.eli5: Imagine a toy set whose pieces snap together. This document describes the pieces and the rules for snapping them, so you can swap one piece for a better one without buying a whole new toy.

sections.title: Design Decisions and Modularity
sections.content:
Several design decisions shape the architecture. It defines subsystems as abstract services, and abstract service interfaces as the boundaries between documents. Each document should be self-contained: the procedures and the MIB objects needed for one portion live together, so that portions can move along the standards track on different time-lines.

The RFC notes that this modularity of specification is not meant to impose any specific requirement on how implementations are built. Remote configuration is another decision: the security and access control subsystems add many new parameters and need frequent changes of secrets, so these parameters must be remotely configurable. Finally, complexity is controlled so that simple devices can use few resources while larger configurations can extend the simple one.

A subsystem is an abstract and incomplete specification of one portion of a framework. A model is a specific, implementable design of a subsystem. An implementation instantiates a subsystem conforming to one or more models.
sections.eli5: The plan says what each room is for, but not how to build it. Different builders can build a room their own way as long as the doors line up.

sections.title: The SNMP Entity and Its Engine
sections.content:
An SNMP entity is an implementation of the architecture. It consists of one SNMP engine plus one or more applications, and there is a one-to-one association between an engine and its entity. The engine is identified by an snmpEngineID, which is unique within an administrative domain.

The engine contains four parts. The Dispatcher (only one per engine) sends and receives messages on the network, works out the version of each message and hands it to the matching Message Processing Model, and gives applications an abstract interface to send and receive PDUs. The Message Processing Subsystem prepares outgoing messages and extracts data from incoming ones, and may hold several Message Processing Models such as SNMPv3, SNMPv1 and SNMPv2c. The Security Subsystem provides authentication and privacy through one or more Security Models, with the User-Based Security Model as the example. The Access Control Subsystem provides authorization through one or more Access Control Models, with the View-Based Access Control Model as the example.

Applications sit on top and use the engine. The RFC lists five kinds: command generators, command responders, notification originators, notification receivers and proxy forwarders. An entity with command generators or notification receivers is traditionally called a manager; one with command responders or notification originators is traditionally called an agent.
sections.eli5: The engine is like a post office with four desks: one that sorts the mail, one that opens and writes envelopes, one that checks IDs, and one that decides who is allowed to see what. The apps are the people who send and read the letters.

sections.title: Naming Identities and Management Information
sections.content:
The architecture names three kinds of things: entities, identities and management information.

For identities, a principal is the "who" on whose behalf services are provided. A securityName is a human-readable, model-independent string representing a principal. A model-dependent security ID is how one Security Model represents that name, for example a community name or a user name, and the model translates between the two.

For management information, a context is a collection of management information accessible by an SNMP entity. A context is always a subset of a single entity, and the same item can exist in several contexts. A context is identified by a contextEngineID and a contextName; each contextName MUST be unique within an entity. A scopedPDU is a block holding a contextEngineID, a contextName and a PDU.

To identify one item you therefore need the engine, the context name, the object type and the instance. The RFC's example is the description (ifDescr) of device-X's first interface: the snmpEngineID, the contextName device-X, the type ifDescr and the instance 1.
sections.eli5: To find one toy in a huge toy store you need the store, the aisle, the shelf and the spot on the shelf. Contexts are the aisles, and a name tag says who is asking.

sections.title: Security Levels and Threats
sections.content:
The architecture recognizes three securityLevel values, ordered from weakest to strongest: noAuthNoPriv (no authentication, no privacy), authNoPriv (authentication without privacy) and authPriv (authentication with privacy). Every message has a security level, and all subsystems and applications are REQUIRED to supply a value or abide by the supplied one.

Security Models SHOULD protect against two principal threats, modification of information and masquerade, and two secondary ones, message stream modification (re-ordering, delay or replay beyond what the network does naturally) and disclosure. They need not protect against denial of service or traffic analysis, which the RFC deems of lesser importance here.

The Security Considerations section stresses that the level of security depends on the specific Security Model and Access Control Model implementations used, that applications SHOULD take reasonable steps to protect data from disclosure, and that implementations must protect configuration secrets. The MIB module in this RFC has no writable objects.
sections.eli5: There are three kinds of envelopes: a plain postcard, a postcard with a signature, and a sealed signed envelope. The guards mostly worry about people changing, faking or snooping on messages, not about people jamming the mailbox.

sections.title: Abstract Service Interfaces
sections.content:
Section 4 lists primitives, the abstract calls between subsystems. The RFC stresses they describe externally observable behavior and must not be read as APIs or as requirements on how implementations are organized.

The Dispatcher offers applications sendPdu, processPdu, returnResponsePdu and processResponsePdu, plus registerContextEngineID and unregisterContextEngineID so an application can claim responsibility for a context engine and PDU types. The Message Processing Subsystem offers prepareOutgoingMessage, prepareResponseMessage and prepareDataElements. The Security Subsystem offers generateRequestMsg, processIncomingMsg and generateResponseMsg. The Access Control Subsystem offers isAccessAllowed, which takes the security model, name and level, a view type (read, write or notify), the context name and the OID of the object. All subsystems that pass a stateReference also provide stateRelease.

The scenario diagrams show the flow. A command generator calls sendPdu; the Dispatcher asks the Message Processing Model to prepare the message, which asks the Security Model to generate it; the response later travels back the same way to processResponsePdu. A command responder first registers its contextEngineID, then receives processPdu and answers with returnResponsePdu.
sections.eli5: Each desk in the post office has a few simple requests it understands, like "please wrap this" or "please check this". The document lists those requests so every desk can talk to every other desk.

sections.title: Frameworks, MIB and IANA Registries
sections.content:
The RFC situates itself among other documents: transport mappings, message processing, security, access control, protocol operations, applications, the Structure of Management Information, textual conventions, conformance statements and MIB modules. PDUs are grouped into classes such as Read, Write, Response, Notification, Internal, Confirmed and Unconfirmed. It also summarizes SNMPv1, SNMPv2, SNMPv2c and SNMPv3; SNMPv3 adds a new message format, message security, access control and remote configuration.

Section 5 defines the SNMP-FRAMEWORK-MIB, a set of managed objects that instrument the entities. Section 6 creates three IANA-managed number spaces: security models (0 to 255, with 0 reserved for 'any', 1 for SNMPv1, 2 for SNMPv2c and 3 for the User-Based Security Model), message processing models (0 to 255, with 0 for SNMPv1, 1 for SNMPv2c, 2 for SNMPv2u and SNMPv2*, and 3 for SNMPv3), and SnmpEngineID formats (the fifth octet carries a format identifier, with IANA managing values 6 to 127).

Appendix A gives design guidelines for authors of new security models, message processing models, applications and access control models.
sections.eli5: There is a numbered list of which kind of lock, envelope and message style is which, so everyone uses the same numbers for the same thing.
